sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 485 ± 20.7 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface trafficking to plasma membrane confirmed in CHO cells (L1, PMC8414166). Signaling function NOT MEASURED in L1. Caution: L4 (PMC8872787, different paper, different construct) reports that N-terminal 3xFLAG-3xHA tags on PROKR2 abolish MAPK/Egr1-luciferase signaling in HEK293T cells; the 2-HA tag in L1 is smaller and from a different study.
sites.rationale: PROKR2 is a GPCR with an extracellular N-terminal domain (residues 1-53, 53 residues clear of TM1 at position 54) and an intracellular C-terminus (residues 336-384). L1 reports a full-length, membrane-anchored PROKR2 N-terminally fused to 2-HA tags expressed in CHO cells, with surface trafficking confirmed. Because the C-terminus is intracellular, the N-terminal prepend (insert_after_residue=0) is the only extracellular terminus and the position is topology-derived. Confidence is low because L4 (a separate paper) shows that a larger N-terminal tag (3xFLAG-3xHA) abolishes PROKR2 signaling, raising concern that any N-terminal tag may perturb function. Full-length PROKR2 N-terminally fused to 2-HA tags expressed in CHO cells (PMC8414166); construct used to assess importance of N7 and N27 glycosylation for receptor trafficking. The N-terminus (residues 1-53) is extracellular per topology landmarks; C-terminus is intracellular, leaving the N-terminal prepend as the sole extracellular terminus. No specific residue number is named in L1; position is topology-derived.

sources.claim: To assess the importance of glycosylation at N7 and N27 of PKR2 for receptor trafficking, PKR2, PKR2-N7Q, PKR2-N27Q, and PKR2-N7/27Q N-terminally fused to 2-HA tags were transfected in CHO cells.

literature_notes: L2 (PMC8872787) reports a cell-surface biotinylation assay for PROKR2-3xHA constructs but does not specify whether the 3xHA tag is at the N- or C-terminus independently of L3; L3 clarifies that both N-terminal and C-terminal 3F3H constructs were made. L4 (PMC8872787) explicitly shows that C-terminal 3F3H PROKR2 is functional (MAPK signaling preserved) while N-terminal 3F3H PROKR2 is non-functional. The C-terminal tag site (residue 384) is intracellular and is recorded in other_positions. L5 (PMC8872787) describes immunostaining of PROKR2-3F3H in COS-7 cells, consistent with L3/L4 findings. No ledger line supports an internal extracellular loop insertion for PROKR2. The N-terminal site (L1) is reported with low confidence given the conflicting functional data from L4.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal 3xFLAG-3xHA (3F3H) tag on PROKR2; C-terminus is intracellular (residues 336-384 per topology landmarks); tag is functional for MAPK/Egr1 signaling (L4) but faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
